rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 5 (ruling-sam-2026-10-07-p1-008): the prototype wins by default, and claim 6 (p1-011): only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint overrides it; none applies here, and the two prototype positions agree once the code is read whole, so the prototype's '21 June 2026' wins over today's short month name.
outcome: The Design Release 2.1 card writes the arrival date as day, full month name and year, such as '21 June 2026'. The prototype's code and render agree: at 04a073b the card partial (app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/dashboard-notification-card.html) prints arrivalDateDisplay, which formatDashboardArrivalDate (app/routes.js:7201) builds from notification.arrivalDate; it only rewrites a d/m/yyyy value to dd/mm/yyyy and otherwise passes the stored text through. Every value the card receives is already 'D Month YYYY': the seed data in app/data/dashboard-notifications.js stores '21 June 2026', and submitted notifications store formatDateForDashboard(snapshot.arrivalDateAtPort) (app/routes.js:6883, 6989), which writes the full month name via formatDeclarationDate. So the dd/mm/yyyy branch is never reached on the card, and the rendered '21 June 2026' is what the prototype does. Today's card's short month name ('7 Nov 2026') changes to the full month name; no DR1 judgement or real constraint overrides the prototype on this difference.
